episodes.192154: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a boundary moving east across northern Alabama and southern middle Tennessee. Some of these storms produced sporadic wind damage in Morgan county, AL along with a funnel cloud in southwestern Limestone county.
episodes.192177: The monsoon high over northern Arizona on July 19th continued backing west to over the Great Basin July 20th and 21st in response to upper level troughing over the central U.S. The upper level trough over the central U.S. helped bring a backdoor front through eastern NM early on July 20th. In between the two synoptic features, upper level disturbances travelled south through New Mexico. This resulted in a greater coverage of afternoon and evening showers and storms over the region both days with activity slowly waning overnight. Storms over the South Fork burn scar brought another round of flash flooding to the Ruidoso area Saturday afternoon with the Rio Ruidoso rising to a record level of 15.39 feet July 20th. Flash flooding was reported from storms in Portales mid Sunday afternoon. Another round of flash flooding occurred in Ruidoso Sunday night from storms moving south through the area. Daytime heating on Monday resulted in another crop of showers and storms mainly across the higher terrain Monday afternoon and evening moving south with time. Storms produced some flash flooding on the northeast part of the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar and a peak wind gust of 62 mph on the White Sands Missile Range near Oscuro.
episodes.192205: A largely ridge-dominated pattern persisted, resulting in anomalously warm temperatures. These hot temperatures resulted in at least one instance of a heat related fatality. Despite the strong ridge, enough moisture continued to work into the area and help in the development of diurnal convection, some of which resulted in flash flooding over more rain sensitive areas.
episodes.192442: A thunderstorm produced localized gale-force wind gusts over Tangier Sound.
episodes.192580: A large complex of thunderstorms moved over the Tucson Metro resulting in Flash Flooding, especially in the Drexel Heights area. Additionally, several reports of severe threshold wind gusts occurred in the Tucson area and in Nogales.
episodes.192619: Isolated to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed out ahead of a stalled frontal boundary across the Coastal Plain. This activity merged and became multiple linear segments that tracked eastwards across portions of the inland rivers and sounds of eastern North Carolina. Some of these storms within the line became strong in nature producing damaging wind gusts along the Pamlico River.
episodes.192620: Isolated to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along the Crystal Coast during the morning of July 22nd. A few of these storms became strong in nature producing damaging wind gusts across the Coastal Waters along the Crystal Coast.
episodes.192774: High pressure system moved further southwest and created a weak flow pattern over Nevada, leaving excess moisture brought in from the system when it was over the four corners, producing afternoon thunderstorms that caused high outflow winds.
episodes.192776: A midlevel impulse sparked slow moving scattered showers and thunderstorms, which resulted in urban flash flooding and a severe wind gust.
episodes.192800: Isolated shower and thunderstorm chances returned 20 July, and remained mostly south of Highway 50 with Mono-Mineral Counties being the focal points for activity. High-resolution ensemble guidance also showed the best chances for showers and thunderstorms mostly south of highway 50. Simulations projected a 30-40% chance for isolated showers and a few storms that would initiate mostly across Mono, southern Lyon, and Mineral counties around 1-2PM. There was also a chance (10-20%) that one or two storms would push northeast into eastern Churchill County as well. Storms quickly tapered off in the evening after sundown. Afternoon west-southwest breezes of 20-30 mph were expected to be slightly enhanced  in the vicinity of developing storms. The usual storm related culprits of copious lightning, as well as gusty and erratic outflows accompanied storms across the area.

episodes.192958: An upper-level low pressure system was the driving force of scattered storms across Central New York. Warm, moist air became unstable enough for isolated severe storms. These storms had strong wind gusts that knocked over trees and wires in Tioga and Broome Counties. Small hail was also observed.
episodes.192959: An upper-level low pressure system was the driving force of scattered storms across Northeastern Pennsylvania. Warm, moist air became unstable enough for isolated severe storms. These storms had strong wind gusts that knocked over trees and wires in Bradford County.
episodes.193068: In the midst of a stationary frontal boundary promoting showers and storms across West Virginia on the morning of July 22nd, an isolated instance of flash flooding occurred in the Beckley area of West Virginia. Heavy rainfall accompanying convective activity early that morning yielded minor creek flooding in Raleigh County, which spilled onto Robert C Byrd Drive where it intersects with Ewart Avenue. High water issues dragged on into the morning rush hour before gradually tapering down in response to the creek returning to its banks.
episodes.193247: A SSE flow focused the east coast sea breeze inland with a merger of sea breezes across the interior of NE FL during the late afternoon. A few strong to pulse severe storms produced wind damage and locally heavy rain.
episodes.193401: An area of low pressure over the lower Ohio Valley tracked into the Mid-Atlantic states along a stalled frontal boundary over Virginia. The track of the surface low led to the development of afternoon and evening isolated to scattered showers and storms, primarily along and east of the US Highway 1 corridor. These storm cells at times produced damaging wind reports, including downed trees, as well as flash flooding across Sampson, Wake, Durham, and Franklin Counties. Storm activity waned by the late evening hours.
episodes.193470: Numerous reports of flash flooding north of Columbia due to training thunderstorms with extremely high rain rates. Moderate instability, weak but parallel mid-level flow to the low level moisture convergence axis, and precipitable water values over 2.1 inches caused several hours with 2-3 inch per hour rain fall rates. Several locations exceeded 3 inch per hour rates and totals exceeded 5 inches locally.
episodes.193800: Increasing moisture and instability ahead of a tropical wave over the Bahamas led to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms over the Atlantic waters off South Florida on the evening of July 21st.
episodes.194147: An area of low pressure and associated frontal boundary slowly moved from north to south across the region on the 22nd. Showers and thunderstorms developed along the boundary and moved to the east. No strong or severe storms were observed, but the storms did produce heavy rainfall in isolated areas. One of the storms caused minor flash flooding in Phillips where storm drains were overwhelmed and water started flowing into an ambulance garage.
episodes.194328: An upper trough draped across the central and eastern U.S. and a stalled front over Central Texas combined to generated scattered showers and thunderstorms July 21 through July 23. Most of the storms remained sub-severe, but a few generated heavy rain and flash flooding in some locations, and one storm produced a damaging microburst in Hood County on the 21st.
episodes.194393: Evening thunderstorms developed primarily in Tennessee near a stationary boundary, with one storm deviating northward through Calloway County, Kentucky. This storm produced several reports of wind damage and resulted in a water rescue being needed in Murray as torrential rain induced flash flooding. MLCAPE was around 1000 J/kg and effective bulk shear was very limited, while PWs were near 1.8 inch.
episodes.194467: Modest moisture remained across the region with an upper level disturbance moving through northerly flow aloft.  This disturbance triggered a severe thunderstorm east of Deming and some flash flooding around the Truth or Consequences area.
episodes.194484: A cluster of thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze in the afternoon and remained nearly stationary across Chatham County. This cluster of thunderstorms produced extremely heavy rainfall across portions of Chatham County, with the heaviest rain occurring in the Savannah area. Approximately 3 to 5 inches of rain was measured at several automated rain gauge sites, with most of the rain falling in a 1 to 2 hour period of time. Numerous roads were flooded and closed in Savannah due to the heavy rain. One flash flood event occurred as well, with water entering the first floor of an apartment building.
episodes.194517: With the subtropical high pressure centered near Las Vegas, Nevada, the overall steering flow was from the north to northeast. Strong daytime heating in combination with PWAT values of 1.5+ inches resulted in MLCAPE values in excess of 1000 J/KG and DCAPE values in excess of 1500 J/KG. In addition, in the upper-levels, there was a disturbance that helped with the vertical ascent. As a result, the environment was primed for the development of strong to severe thunderstorms. Strong thunderstorm activity developed across the Mogollon Rim during the late morning into the early afternoon hours and was steered southwestward towards south-central AZ. A deep, long traveling outflow boundary developed and surged well ahead of the activity and traversed the entire Phoenix metro area with strong winds as well as areas of blowing dust during the mid to late afternoon hours. The outflow boundary as it continued to migrate southward sparked additional thunderstorm activity across portions of northwest Pinal and southwest Maricopa Counties.
episodes.194559: A west to east oriented front along with a passing shortwave trough provided the energy and forcing for a severe thunderstorm to develop over Erie County. The storm was short lived and weakened as it tracked southeast into neighboring Wyoming County. One report was received for each severe hail and thunderstorm wind damage.
episodes.194591: Heavy rainfall and flash flooding on July 20 and 21 in El Paso and Pueblo Counties.
episodes.194616: A wet microburst occurred in association with a strong thunderstorm moving north around 25 mph over the upper portion of Plantation Key. A small-scale elongated swath of wind damage to trees and lose, small to medium-sized yard objects occurred. Power outages, secondary damages to parked vehicles due to falling large tree limbs occurred with estimated straight-line wind gusts between 60 and 85 mph.  Post-analysis indicated a pronounced layer of dry mid-level air with both convective instability and downburst potential well above climatological normal for July.
episodes.194761: Evening thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce a water spout offshore Venice in Sarasota County and strong marine wind gusts in the Tampa Bay and Sarasota Bay areas.
episodes.194778: Main hazards were hail and wind in Northeastern North Dakota and Northwestern Minnesota.
episodes.194779: Main hazards were hail and wind in Northeastern North Dakota and Northwestern Minnesota.
episodes.194834: Low pressure aloft over the Great Lakes featured a southward moving surface cold front located across central MN and western WI. A line of thunderstorms developed during the evening of July 22nd and produced strong winds.
episodes.194904: Areas of slow-moving thunderstorms and storm clusters developed across western North Carolina during the evening. Very heavy rain falling in a short period of time resulted in flash flooding across Henderson County and on the north side of Charlotte.
episodes.194908: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina mountains during the afternoon. One of the storms produced a couple of strong downbursts near the border of Buncombe and Madison Counties.
episodes.194915: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed in southwest Panola County early in the afternoon on July 22nd. This thunderstorm produced very localized damaging wind gusts, consistent with that of a microburst. Damage at a single residence included numerous trees branches snapped, an outdoor table destroyed, and an awning was ripped off of a trailer just off of FM Road 1971 on County Road 164 in the Dotson/Long Branch area.
episodes.194936: An upper-level low pressure system was the driving force of scattered storms across Northeast Pennsylvania. Warm and moist air contributed to several rounds of heavy rain producing thunderstorms over the northern tier counties. Rainfall amounts in a short period of time totalled between 2 and 3 inches leading to localized flash flooding.
episodes.194938: An upper-level low pressure system was the driving force of scattered storms across Central New York. Warm and moist air contributed to several rounds of heavy rain producing thunderstorms over the Central Southern Tier. Rainfall amounts in a short period of time totalled between 2 and 3 inches leading to localized flash flooding.
episodes.194974: Monsoon moisture advecting around the periphery of the big ridge causing excessive heat fueled scattered thunderstorms. Several storms produced high winds and/or flooding.
episodes.194976: Monsoon moisture trapped under the big ridge causing excessive heat fueled isolated thunderstorms. A few storms produced high winds and/or flooding.
episodes.195145: Scattered thunderstorms produced gusty winds as they moved across the James River on July 22, 2024.
episodes.195147: A moist air mass was in place with dew points generally in the mid 70s on July 22, 2024. This resulted in heavy rain and localized flooding across portions of eastern and southeastern Virginia.
episodes.195148: Scattered thunderstorms produced gusty winds as they moved across the Chesapeake Bay on July 22, 2024.
episodes.195153: Deep monsoon moisture over northern Arizona porduced severe thundertorms with damaging winds and flash flooding.
episodes.195225: A stationary front was draped across central Kentucky, with waves of showers and thunderstorms moving along and north of this front on July 22nd. During the early morning hours, a cluster of slow-moving storms produced heavy rainfall which resulted in flash flooding across parts of Barren County. Another wave of showers and storms later in the afternoon produced scattered wind damage across Warren County, with more localized flash flooding being observed in Breckinridge County.

A remote NWS storm survey in consultation with the Village of Islamorada Emergency Manager and several residents, social media videos and photos, as well as in-situ review of realtime Florida Department of Transportation video revealed a wet microburst occurred in the upper Plantation Key area of the Indian Mounds Trail neighborhood.  Estimated wind gusts of 60 to 85 mph occurred over an area about one to one and a half miles wide by two miles long as the microburst began on the oceanside of the Old Overseas Highway.  The straight-line winds associated with the microburst crossed U.S. Highway 1 into the Indian Mounds Trail Neighborhood.  Numerous large trees and tree tops were downed in an area over 5 blocks long, with secondary damages to several vehicles and a broken window of one residence.  Lighter but sizable yard objects including furniture, trash receptacles were tossed one or more lots downwind, with one trampoline lofted into a tree.  Several of the neighborhood streets were temporarily impassible due to the size of the tree limbs.  Some minor fascia and shingle damage was also noted at a few residences.  Approximately 1,100 residents were without power as the tree limbs downed utility lines, with one tree partially blocking northbound U.S. Highway 1.
Weather Station at Forte Shores Dr. reported a wind gust of 47 knots as thunderstorms were moving through the area. Report was relayed through WeatherFlow.
A microburst knocked down and split trees south and southwest of Tolar. A barn and storage container were also damaged.

Rainfall amounts of around half an inch over the South Fork burn scar resulted in more flash flooding across the Upper Canyon and Brady Canyon neighborhoods west of downtown Ruidoso. Runoff on the burn scar resulted in flash flooding on the Rio Ruidoso resulting in road closures along and near the banks of the river, including White Mountain and Sunny Slope Drive, Brady Canyon Road and Mechem from Cedar Creek, and Gavilan Canyon Road. Property damage is an estimate.
